_comment: Map markers whose wiki article is spelled differently from ours.
The join is marker.article -> location.wiki_page, and 27 of 46 match on
their own. These three do not, and each is a real difference rather than a
typo, so they are written down with the reason instead of being absorbed by
a fuzzy matcher.
ANCHORS ONLY. An entry here says 'this marker is that location's position'.
It does not create a location, and a marker with no entry and no matching
page is left alone rather than attached to whatever is nearest — geometric
containment would be an inference, and this file is for facts.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. The five mine biomes have no anchor and never
will: a biome is a range of floors, not a place on the overworld, so its
position is *not applicable* rather than unknown. The Bell Tower has no
marker and stays an honest gap. Balor's Wagon DOES have a fixed pitch —
the game's own rm_town.tmx places the wagon object in town, contrary to
this file's earlier guess that a travelling merchant might have none —
but the wiki map still carries no marker for it, so its hand-placed
anchor lives in curated/maps/markers.json and ships inferred.
QUESTS. The wiki's seven Quest-group markers are barriers: broken bridges
and stairs, sealed caves. Two name a quest we hold nearly word for word
and are linked below. The other five are NOT linked, on purpose: no quest
record of ours matches 'Sealed Beach Cave', the stairs or the vine by
name, and deducing that a marker is the door a given seal opens would be
a guess wearing a link. They ship as quest-kind spots with quest_id null.

quests.reason: Exact name match: the quest is 'Repair the Beach Bridge' and the marker sits on the beach.
The quest is 'Repair the Bridge'. We hold exactly two bridge-repair quests; the other names the beach, and this marker is on the Eastern Road, not the beach.

anchors.reason: The marker links to the article 'Farm'; our page is 'The_Farm'. Same place, two spellings.
The marker links to 'Mines'; our page is 'The_Mines'.

The gardens have no marker of their own. The gazebo stands in them and is the only published point inside them, so it serves as the anchor — the pin is a few metres off centre, which is well inside the accuracy this map claims anyway.
